label: 07 · The unified thesis
html:
07 · The unified thesis

AIO + GEO + AEO = strengthening an entity's prominence & knowledge graph

Which is what SEO has always been about. The acronyms are new. The discipline is not.

In plain English: an entity's prominence is how loudly it shows up across the web when AI looks for an answer in a topic. The knowledge graph is the web of "this thing relates to that thing" AI uses to decide what's authoritative. AIO + GEO + AEO all push that same engine.

AIO

AI responses

Visibility in ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Perplexity. Map each AI's semantic borders for a topic and optimize so you appear in responses to your core queries.

GEO

Future training

AIs are months behind. Trusted sources + outreach + quality writing create favorable word co-occurrence in the next training set.

AEO

Retrieval queries

The query paths AI agents use to ground answers (Copilot→Bing, Perplexity→Google, DeepSeek→Baidu). Optimize the questions they ask.

label: 08 · Old SEO vs Modern SEO
html:
08 · Old SEO vs Modern SEO

Same craft. Different surface.

The technical foundations don't change. What changes is the distribution: AI agents now read your website the same way Google did ten years ago.

5 - 10 years ago

  • Stuff the keyword “wellness resort Switzerland” 50 times
  • Make the homepage look attractive
  • Optimize for Google visibility only
  • Buy backlinks from any directory that would publish them
  • Measure: ranking position

Now

  • Write valuable articles: “Why a Swiss Alps wellness retreat is worth the journey”, “What does a 5-star spa program actually include?”, “Best time of year for a lake-view wellness stay”
  • Create content that answers questions at every stage of the journey
  • Optimize so Google + ChatGPT + Gemini + Perplexity all understand your expertise and recognize your brand
  • Earn citations from authoritative travel, wellness, Swiss hospitality publications
  • Measure: AI mentions, citations, direct bookings
Same craft. Different surface. Crawlability, structured data, content depth, authority signals - none of this changes. What changes is the distribution: AI agents now read your website the same way Google did ten years ago.

label: 10 · AIO

10 · AIO
Visibility in AI responses

AIO - Artificial Intelligence Optimization

Be present across the full model landscape - ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Perplexity, DeepSeek, Meta, plus the open-source wave (Kimi, Minimax, Qwen, GLM).

Each AI has its own semantic borders - the boundaries of what it considers “this topic” and what it considers “out of scope.” Optimizing for AIO means mapping those borders across every model your guests might ask and producing content that sits squarely inside each one’s frame, so your brand surfaces in responses to your core queries regardless of which AI is answering.

What we do: identify the top 30–50 query intents in your space, query each AI (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Perplexity, DeepSeek, Meta, Kimi, Minimax, Qwen, GLM) to see who gets cited, reverse-engineer the corpus each model uses, and produce the missing content clusters.
What we measure: AI Overview mentions, ChatGPT / Perplexity / Gemini / Claude / DeepSeek / Meta citations, Kimi / Minimax / Qwen / GLM presence (the open-source wave), share-of-voice vs named competitors (Bürgenstock, The Dolder Grand, Bad Ragaz, etc.).
Example query
“Recommend a luxury spa resort near Zurich with lake and mountain views for a couple”
Without AIO: AI names 3 competitors, never Panorama.
With AIO: Panorama is one of the three - and the citation traces to your own site.

label: 11 · GEO
html:
11 · GEO
Influence the next training cycle

GEO - Generative Engine Optimization

AIs are months behind - that's the opportunity. But each model has its own preferences based on training data, so strategies are nuanced per target.

A large language model is only as current as its training cut-off. ChatGPT-5, Gemini 2, Claude 4, Qwen, Kimi - each was trained on a different corpus with different preferences: travel verticals, encyclopedic sources, news outlets, niche authorities, regional publishers. How that corpus is shaped determines what the AI favors in responses for years.

GEO starts with the answer the AI is already giving. We find the cited sources behind today's responses, identify which authoritative domains each model preferentially cites, and reverse-engineer the content network needed to win that model's next training cycle. Outreach lists, publication targets, and co-occurrence strategies are nuanced per target - what shapes Claude's corpus is not what shapes Qwen's or Kimi's.

What we do: per-LLM cited-source mapping, per-target PR outreach (Forbes Travel Guide, Condé Nast Traveller, Wellness Magazin for Western models; Chinese travel press and Quark-cited sources for Qwen / Kimi), digital PR in high-trust domains, structured data future scrapers will see.
What we measure: share-of-voice in each model's training-corpus-relevant domains, citation velocity in those sources, semantic-association lift per target model.
Tactic example
Forbes Travel Guide, Condé Nast Traveller, Wellness Magazin

One Panorama feature in each, anchored to “best Swiss wellness resorts 2026,” means the next training cycle bakes that association in - for the next 12 - 24 months of model responses.

label: 12 · AEO
html:
12 · AEO
Optimize the query paths agents use

AEO - Answer Engine Optimization

AIs aren't current. They need a retrieval layer to ground their answers - and each model uses a different index.

When an AI says “as of…” or cites a webpage, it's because a retrieval system fetched it. Each model uses a different search index:

  • Claude → Brave Search
  • Grok → Bing
  • ChatGPT → Bing + proprietary search crawler
  • Qwen → Quark Search
  • Kimi → Moonshot search
  • OpenClaw / Hermes Agent → configurable - Tavily, SerperAPI, SERPAPI, Firecrawl

AEO is query-path optimization at its core: understanding what each agent is likely to ask about a topic, ensuring the answers are findable, fresh, and structured for machine consumption on the specific index that model pulls from.

What we do: per-retrieval-engine source study, schema.org & FAQPage markup, freshness signals, content designed to answer the questions each index actually serves.
What we measure: retrieval-source citations per engine (Brave for Claude, Bing for ChatGPT / Grok / Kimi, Quark for Qwen, configurable for OpenClaw / Hermes), answer-engine inclusion rates.
Tactic example
“Bürgenstock vs Panorama Resort & Spa”

A user asks AI to compare. Without AEO, AI cites only Booking.com and TripAdvisor. With AEO, AI cites panoramaresort.ch directly - because the structured comparison page on your site is the cleanest answer.

✅ What's working

❌ What's missing in AI

  • Visible in only 2.4% of prompts
  • Of 26 prompts assessed: 25 returned 0% visibility. Only one branded prompt (queries mentioning Panorama by name) yielded recognition, at 20% visibility. The 25 unbranded prompts - the kind real travelers use - return zero citations.

The issue is that AI indexes favor HTML pages over PDFs - several core pages (spa menu, rooms overview, culinary brochure) currently exist only as PDFs, which means AI can't read them. Converting those PDFs to indexable HTML pages is one of the highest-leverage quick wins.

19 · Plan of action

Plan of action

Sequenced by dependency. The order matters: technical foundations first, content second, authority third, measurement throughout. All language work is German + English (your priority markets).
01
Technical audit & retrieval hygiene
Schema markup (Organization, LocalBusiness, FAQPage, HowTo, Offer). Heading, meta, URL hygiene. Internal linking overhaul so authority flows toward the wellness weekend offer.
02
Topical map & AI corpus study
50 query intents in the Swiss luxury wellness space. Per-AI corpus mapping (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Perplexity, Meta). Identify the missing content clusters that make Panorama citeable.
03
Structured answer pages & comparison content
30+ pages designed to be retrieved, parsed and cited directly. Comparison pages (vs Bürgenstock, Dolder Grand, Bad Ragaz). FAQPage + HowTo schema on each. German first, English second.
04
Off-site authority & digital PR
Outreach to Forbes Travel Guide, Condé Nast Traveller, Wellness Magazin, Schweizer Illustrierte. Authoritative backlinks aligned with the co-occurrence terms that feed next training cycle. Wikipedia entity + Wikidata graph.
05
Measurement & continuous refinement
Monthly dashboard: AI Overview share, ChatGPT/Perplexity/Gemini citation rate, share-of-voice vs named competitors, direct bookings, OTA commission saved. Quarterly strategy review.
Cadence: 90-day first cycle to demonstrate traction · Month-to-month after Q1 · Quarterly strategy reviews
